facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s with a history of recent hospitalization for congestive heart failure
developed a painful ulceration on the right distal forearm at a previous peripheral intravenous catheter site
The ulceration appeared a few days after discharge
cleaning her fish tank, playing with her pet cat, and gardening in her indoor cactus garden
No recent travel history or immunosuppressive medications were reported
The patient was readmitted for bacterial pneumonia
ulcerated plaque on the right forearm with 2 tender, 1- to 2-cm red nodules in the right antecubital fossa
marked superficial and deep inflammation composed predominantly of neutrophils with associated tissue necrosis
Multiple filamentous gram-positive bacilli identified on Gram stain
Ziehl Nielson, Fite, and periodic acid–Schiff stains were negative for organisms
Tissue culture: Positive for specific organism
